newsitem.title: UK: UK supermarket shares rebound but worries persist.
newsitem.headline: UK supermarket shares rebound but worries persist.

text.p: Worries about Tesco's latest "unbeatable value campaign" continued to overhang the supermarket sector on Thursday with BZW warning that downgrades in the sector are a distinct possibility, market sources said.
Shares in the sector largely rebounded after Wednesday's announcement with Tesco adding 3-1/2p to 294-1/2p, Safeway 5p to 328p and ASDA 1/2p to 106-1/2p.
Sainsbury, however, dipped again losing 3p to 373-1/2p.
BZW was said to be worried that Tesco's move represented a repositioning not a promotion and as such could have serious ramifications for the sector.

BZW will review its forecasts next week when more information on the promotion will be available and while it remains long term positive on Safeway, Tesco and ASDA it is temporarily suspending its "buy" stance, the sources said.
Of the three, it identifies ASDA as the most vulnerable.
BZW anlayst David McCarthy was not immediately available to comment.
